guideline: Keyboard focus.

Individual avatars inside Avata

fields.before: An avatar group displays a set of related avatars together. It’s typically used to represent a collection of people or entities.
fields.after:
Keyboard focus.

Individual avatars inside Avatar group can be navigated using a keyboard. The keyboard focus state adds a focus ring around the avatar.

entries.name: guideline: Adjusting stroke color to match neutral backgrou

fields.before: Avatar sizes scale exponentially, based on the Spectrum type scale. Avatar has preset sizes to flex across all surfaces and can also be customized to fit appropriately for your context.
fields.after:
Adjusting stroke color to match neutral backgrounds.

Each individual avatar has a stroke applied to better show distinction between individual users in the group. By default, the outline color is a neutral gray, but the stroke color should be adjusted manually to match the background where the avatar group is placed.

entries.name: guideline: An Avatar group can have an optional text label

before.content: An Avatar group can have an optional text label that clearly describes the group or number of users that it represents.

source.title: feat(design-data): anatomy review of the groups family (A6)

before.name: avatar
before.description: One avatar in the overlapping stack.

after.name: avatars
after.description: Overlapping stack of avatars. It hosts the default slot; each avatar is one fill, drawn overlapping the previous one.

after.name: container
after.description: Row holding the overlapping avatars and the optional label. It is the root.

fields.before: Text label such as the member count; optional via Show label.
fields.after: Text label next to the stack, such as the member count; optional via the label option.

fields.before: Figma S2 Web avatar group page (Stack of Avatar instances plus Label text). Relationship contexts mention a layout and a group-to-label spacing that were not made parts.
fields.after: Figma S2 Web avatar group page (all 7 size variants: a frame named Stack holding the Avatar instances, plus a Label, which matches the avatars host) and React Spectrum S2 AvatarGroup. The repeated avatars sit in one host part, avatars (A142); the avatar is what the default slot accepts, so avatar is no longer a part. An explicit container is the root. The avatar to avatar and avatar group to label spacings are now spacings between these parts.
